children: By Utkarsh    Hathi and Ragini Mathur

The tech-heavy Nasdaq gained in choppy trading on Wednesday as investors weighed Nvidia's upbeat forecast against uncertainty over the pricing of Anthropic's IPO, while hawkish remarks from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller added to the pressure.
Nvidia

shares fell 1.6%, with a strong forecast from the chip bellwether doing little to lift investor sentiment. Uncertainty around Nvidia's outlook following former CEO Jensen Huang's sudden exit last week has rattled investor confidence in the AI trade.
The company said on Tuesday it expects fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%. Analysts on average had estimated $125.25 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

"The central question Nvidia faces is not related to this earnings report ... it's more about what the company may look like in 3-5 years without a visionary leader like Jensen and as competition from other chipmakers takes shape," said Jay Peters, portfolio manager at NewEdge Wealth.
Nvidia's board dismissed the idea of rehiring Huang amid a campaign to bring him back.
Chip stocks were mixed, though the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index
was last up 0.7%.

Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve's Waller told CNBC on Wednesday that the central bank needs to either approve a half-point interest rate hike at its December meeting or communicate a faster pace of hikes in 2027.
"That's (a half-point hike) only going to serve to accelerate the math on value compression and then that starts to hurt companies," said Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion.
Investors will scan the minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee's October meeting, due later on Wednesday, for clues on the central bank's policy path.
Traders are almost fully pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike next month, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.
At 12:36 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average
fell 372.72 points, or 0.73%, to 50,386.70, the S&P 500
CBOE:SPX
gained 0.73 points, or 0.01%, to 7,341.26 and the Nasdaq Composite
gained 129.52 points, or 0.54%, to 24,460.40.
Five of 11 major S&P 500 sectors were in negative territory, with the energy sector
leading losses, down 2.6%, as oil prices slipped more than 1% after US crude and fuel inventories posted larger-than-expected rises.
The consumer discretionary sector
gained 2.4%.
SPOTLIGHT ON ANTHROPIC
With Nvidia's results out of the way, attention is shifting to the pricing of Anthropic's
initial public offering later in the day, a key test of Wall Street's appetite for companies tied to the AI boom.
The Claude chatbot creator is eyeing a valuation of as much as $1.4 trillion in what would be the first IPO by a frontier AI model developer.
Neocloud stocks were mixed, with CoreWeave
down 2.4%, while Nebius
Among other movers, off-price retailer TJX
jumped 11% after forecasting upbeat annual sales, banking on strong demand ahead of the holiday shopping season.
Target
shares gained 6.8% after the retailer reported a third straight quarter of better-than-expected results as its recovery takes root.
Take-Two Interactive
shares gained 7.4% as the global rollout of its Grand Theft Auto VI video game was set to begin on Wednesday.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.05-to-1 ratio on the NYSE, and by a 1.22-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.
The S&P 500 posted 3 new 52-week highs and 7 new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 20 new highs and 348 new lows.
